title: Use pan lids and kitchen exhaust while cooking
why: Lids and an exhaust fan remove cooking smoke and fumes near the source before they spread through the home.

title: Wet mop instead of dry sweeping
why: Dry sweeping can stir settled dust back into the air; a damp mop picks it up instead.

title: Avoid mosquito coils and incense indoors
why: Lab tests found burning one mosquito coil released as much PM2.5 as burning 75-137 cigarettes. Incense is also a burning smoke source indoors.
source: Liu et al. 2003, Environmental Health Perspectives 111(12):1454-1460 (mosquito coils)

title: Don't burn leaves or household trash
why: Burning leaves and trash releases smoke at ground level, right where you and your neighbours breathe.

title: Carpool or take public transport for school and office runs
why: When several people share one vehicle, fewer vehicles make the same trips.

title: Switch from wood, dung or coal stoves to LPG or induction
why: WHO guidelines recommend moving households from polluting solid fuels to clean fuels like LPG and electricity.
source: WHO Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality: Household Fuel Combustion (2014)

title: Use a doormat and leave outdoor shoes outside
why: Leaving outdoor shoes outside cuts the street dust carried into the home.

title: Switch off the engine when waiting
why: An engine running while standing still burns fuel and makes exhaust without taking you anywhere.

title: Use air recirculation in heavy traffic
why: In-car studies found the lowest inside-to-road particle ratios with windows closed and air on recirculate. On long drives, let in fresh air now and then, because CO2 builds up on full recirculation.
source: Hudda et al. 2012, Atmospheric Environment (in-vehicle ultrafine particles); Jung et al. 2017, Atmospheric Environment 160:77-88 (CO2 build-up)

title: Keep windows shut during the smoggiest hours
why: Closed windows let less outdoor smog inside. One study measured indoor PM2.5 at about 63% of outdoor levels with windows closed.
source: Cyrys et al. 2004, J Expo Anal Environ Epidemiol 14(4)

title: Air rooms briefly in the cleanest forecast hour
why: Brief airing still clears cooking fumes and stale air; doing it in the cleanest forecast hour lets in the least smog.
